narrator.name: John
narrator.note: John the apostle on Patmos, telling in the first person what he saw and heard; grave, awed.

angel.name: A strong angel
angel.note: A mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice before the throne.

elder-of-heaven.name: One of the ancients
elder-of-heaven.note: One of the twenty-four ancients, consoling John; gentle and assured.

ancients.name: The twenty-four ancients
ancients.note: The twenty-four crowned ancients around the throne, adoring and singing together.

living-creatures.name: The four living creatures
living-creatures.note: The four winged living creatures about the throne, unceasing in praise; unearthly, resonant.

heavenly-voices.name: Voices of heaven
heavenly-voices.note: Myriads of angels and every creature praising together with a loud voice.

1.t: And I saw, in the right hand of him that sat on the throne, a book, written within and without, sealed with seven seals.

2.t: And I saw a strong angel, proclaiming with a loud voice:
Who is worthy to open the book and to loose the seals thereof?

3.t: And no man was able, neither in heaven nor on earth nor under the earth, to open the book, nor to look on it.

4.t: And I wept much, because no man was found worthy to open the book, nor to see it.

5.t: And one of the ancients said to me:
Weep not: behold the lion of the tribe of Juda, the root of David, hath prevailed to open the book and to loose the seven seals thereof.

6.t: And I saw: and behold in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures and in the midst of the ancients, a Lamb standing, as it were slain, having seven horns and seven eyes: which are the seven Spirits of God, sent forth into all the earth.

7.t: And he came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat on the throne.

8.t: And when he had opened the book, the four living creatures and the four and twenty ancients fell down before the Lamb, having every one of them harps and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints.

9.t: And they sung a new canticle, saying:
Thou art worthy, O Lord, to take the book and to open the seals thereof: because thou wast slain and hast redeemed us to God, in thy blood, out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation:
9.q: sung by the four living creatures and the ancients together; given to the ancients, who hold the harps and are the 'redeemed ... kingdom and priests'

10.t: And hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests, and we shall reign on the earth.

11.t: And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the living creatures and the ancients (and the number of them was thousands of thousands),

12.t: The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive power and divinity and wisdom and strength and honour and glory and benediction.
12.q: many angels, thousands of thousands, speaking as one: treated as a multitude rather than a single angel

13.t: And every creature which is in heaven and on the earth and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, I heard all saying:
To him that sitteth on the throne and to the Lamb, benediction and honour and glory and power, for ever and ever.

14.t: And the four living creatures said:
And the four and twenty ancients fell down on their faces and adored him that liveth for ever and ever.
